Hey Metabunk, was wondering if anyone out there had a sound debunking for this video?

As it stands Youtube has been inundated with these "Strange Sound", videos and almost all of them seem to be commented on and spread by religious end times fanatics of both the Christian and Muslim variety. I was wondering if anyone had anything that could knock the wild speculation back down to earth?

(Note: I actually hold the bible in high esteem but when it comes to the end times I feel that the mainstream interpretation is far too literal. This info really isn't important but I wanted to ensure that readers know I am not starting this thread with any particular agenda other then the truth of the matter.)

http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/story/2013/08/30/bc-terrace-sounds.html

External Quote:

On Friday afternoon city spokesperson Alisa Thompson said she had a simpler explanation — it was a city worker grinding down the blade on a grader.

"The grader blade needed to be straightened. Kind of gets ground down, and it makes a very strange noise. It's as simple as that," said Thompson.

"The video, the YouTube video, is actually right around the corner from the arena, and that's where our employee was doing the straightening."

Voila!

  • #3

It sounds like a slow moving trains wheels rubbing on the tracks and resonating through empty metal box cars. I guessed a sharp curve, an old trellis or a train yard might be the culprit. With that in mind I looked at Terrace, BC on Google maps and sure enough, there's a whole train yard in the middle of town. IMHO, there's no need to look any further than that train yard for the source of that noise.

Edit: Never mind. Looks like Mick's got it. I'll bet that train yard makes some noises of it's own though.

Late add. When it came back in May 2015 two people recorded it at the same time, one from home and one walking toward the Sportsplex lot. The walker's recording gets louder (+5 to +19 dB vs the other one) as they get closer, so the city's grader blade explanation looks right to me. Phone auto gain could inflate that a bit. Spectrograms attached.

In plain terms (requested by some users): the sound gets steadily louder as the person walks toward the Sportsplex, which points to something on the ground near there, not something in the sky.
